newFindings.title: 跨tab刷新失败可清除已轮换的新会话
newFindings.head: 138cf2da1b63195cef7e884f69bdf8ded6ed3c21
newFindings.entrypoint: frontend Axios response interceptor refresh flow after a 401
preconditions: Two same-origin tabs hold the same refresh token in localStorage
Both tabs trigger refresh before either observes the other's update
One request stores the rotated token before the other tab's old-token request fails

source.symbol: refresh failure clears token store and emits session expiry

callPath: Each tab has a distinct module-scoped inflight variable
both can read same refresh token from shared localStorage
one tab rotates and writes new token
its interceptor catch unconditionally clears shared token storage

evidence.limitation: Static cross-tab control-flow inference only; no browser run this turn.

counterevidenceChecked: Single-flight does coalesce requests within one module instance.
No cross-tab lock, broadcast-based refresh coordination, or conditional clear is present in the reviewed tokenStore/http code.
newFindings.observedImpact: An old refresh request that fails after another tab has stored a valid successor can remove that successor from shared localStorage and cause an unnecessary local logout. No unauthorized access gain is established.
newFindings.recommendation: Coordinate rotation across tabs and make failure cleanup conditional on the failed token still being the current token; use server replay tolerance only with an explicit bounded contract.
acceptanceCriteria: In two-browser-context controlled response ordering, a losing old-token response cannot clear a newer stored token.
A genuinely invalid current refresh still clears local session and routes to login.

newFindings.title: 改密或管理员重置未即时撤销已签发access JWT
newFindings.head: 138cf2da1b63195cef7e884f69bdf8ded6ed3c21
preconditions: A user has a still-valid access JWT
That user's password is changed by self-service or administrator reset

source.symbol: self-service password update and refresh-token revocation
admin password reset and refresh-token revocation
JWT authentication checks status but no password/session version

callPath: old access JWT remains cryptographically valid
authenticate verifies JWT and current ACTIVE user but does not compare iat/passwordChangedAt or lookup a session revocation marker

evidence.limitation: Static call-path conclusion. Exact remaining acceptance window depends on deployed access TTL; no request replay was run.

counterevidenceChecked: Disabled/locked users are rejected on each authenticated request.
System role and permissions are reloaded from current DB state per request, so role changes are not frozen in the token.
Refresh tokens are revoked after password update, but access JWTs are not.
newFindings.observedImpact: A holder of an already-issued access token can keep using it for the remaining token lifetime after password change/reset; max duration depends on configured access TTL.
newFindings.recommendation: Define whether password change/reset requires immediate session invalidation. If yes, enforce a session version or server-side revocation contract on each request and keep credential update, refresh revocation, and audit failure semantics recoverable.
acceptanceCriteria: After the chosen contract window, old access and refresh credentials are both rejected following self-change and administrator reset.
New login using the resulting password works and must-change behavior remains enforced according to policy.
pendingQuestions: Confirm whether self-password change and administrator reset must invalidate existing access sessions immediately, and specify the maximum allowed delay.

newFindings.title: 同步更新项目负责人时未同步负责人成员关系
newFindings.head: 138cf2da1b63195cef7e884f69bdf8ded6ed3c21
preconditions: Actor can write the project and has projects.update.
The new managerId differs from the current value.

source.symbol: project generic update has no ProjectMember transfer
HTTP project update transaction upserts new manager and demotes prior manager
project capability resolution requires active ProjectMember except SUPER_ADMIN

callPath: sync project managerId passes writable field whitelist
managerId list visibility can differ from detail/write access resolved via active membership

evidence.limitation: Static comparison: HTTP explicitly synchronizes ProjectMember in same transaction whereas sync updates only Project. No dynamic manager-transfer probe this turn.

counterevidenceChecked: HTTP update's membership transfer is an explicit source-level invariant and transactional side effect.
projectAccess resolves non-SUPER_ADMIN capabilities from active ProjectMember; managerId is a separate visibility condition.
newFindings.observedImpact: Source paths have divergent manager transfer semantics: sync changes Project.managerId without promoting the new manager or demoting the old one; capability resolution still requires active membership. No live request impact was dynamically measured.
newFindings.potentialImpact: The new manager may be listed as able to see the project but lack detail/write access; old manager membership/capabilities can remain. Business policy may define an intentional exception, not found in the reviewed HTTP path.
newFindings.recommendation: Route sync manager transfers through the same transactional command as HTTP, or document and consistently implement a policy allowing a manager without ProjectMember membership.
acceptanceCriteria: Equivalent managerId changes from HTTP and sync leave project.managerId and active ProjectMember roles consistent.
Resolver visibility and capability access for the new and previous manager match the documented policy.
Failure during membership synchronization rolls back the managerId change.
pendingQuestions: Confirm whether managerId is required to imply active MANAGER membership; current HTTP update/create paths implement that relationship.

newFindings.title: 候选风险：数据库 dump 与 uploads 文件快照没有共同恢复点协调
newFindings.head: 138cf2da1b63195cef7e884f69bdf8ded6ed3c21
preconditions: Application writes affecting both file metadata/attachments and uploads can continue during backup collection.

source.symbol: file binaries external to database and relational FileObject metadata

evidence.limitation: The code provides no write barrier/common snapshot identifier; the exact concurrent mutation outcome was not reproduced.

counterevidenceChecked: The script comment says database and uploads should be backed up at the same frequency, but no shared checkpoint or coordinated snapshot mechanism is implemented in this script.
newFindings.observedImpact: 本轮未观察到运行时不一致；仅确认脚本内数据库与文件采集是顺序步骤且没有共享 checkpoint。
newFindings.potentialImpact: 若应用写入在两项采集之间持续运行，配对恢复可能呈现不同状态；实际运行条件和影响尚未证实。
newFindings.recommendation: Bind DB and files to a runId and proven common checkpoint using a write barrier or coordinated versioned snapshots; record dump hash, file manifest hash, and post-restore row/reference/checksum reconciliation.
acceptanceCriteria: An isolated test with adjacent file metadata and binary add/change/delete operations proves a paired restore is coherent, and a mismatched pair/checksum is rejected before acceptance.
pendingQuestions: 确认实际备份期间业务写入是否持续，以及运维平台是否在脚本外提供共同快照/写入屏障；之后用隔离配对恢复演练判定是否形成缺陷。
